- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to historical mean too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Late forecast days (last 5–10) are frequently underestimated, indicating lag in capturing downward momentum.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent spikes; model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility.
- Model underestimates prices when true outcomes show prolonged downward drift after a peak.
- Forecasts often fail to account for seasonal or calendar-based mean reversion patterns (e.g., August dips).
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts rise with recent price spikes but fail to adjust for subsequent corrections.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of corrections after major price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 60+).
- Forecasts are too optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and too pessimistic in the long term (last 10–20 days).
